correctness.rationale: For q≤a every first image is at most a, and the only fixed point there is zero, including the boundary q=a. For q>a every positive fixed point requires a<x<q; its flight time is H(x)=∫_x^{x/q} dz/f(z). H diverges at both endpoints. Writing f(x)=xg(x) with g(z)=r(1−z)(z−a), the sign of H′ is the sign of g(x)−g(x/q), equivalently x+x/q−1−a. The unique minimum is therefore x*=q(1+a)/(1+q), and partial fractions at the two endpoints give the displayed positive logarithmic cutoff. The sign of the map displacement on (a,q) is the sign of T−H(x); off that interval the displacement is negative except at zero. The increasing map preserves each side of any fixed point, so this sign pattern proves the full basins, including x_0=0 and x_0=1, and excludes nontrivial cycles. At the fold, q f(y*)/f(x*)=1 and ∂_T P_T(x*)=q f(y*)>0. Differentiating the first-variation formula once gives P″=(f′(y*)−f′(x*))/f(x*)<0, with the stated rational coefficient −2/P″. Taylor expansion and telescoping reciprocals of the positive forward-iterate deviations give the n(x_n−x*) limit. A fresh ODE integration at (a,q,r)=(0.37,0.78,1.3) gave the claimed tangency and critical scale (finite-difference estimate 0.476473858 versus formula 0.476473842).
residual_risks: The proof text says 'twice differentiating' the first-variation identity; the equation is correct and follows by differentiating it once. The coefficient is for forward iteration from above, not inverse iteration. The population dynamics are deterministic, not a statistical claim about fisheries.

originality.rationale: The distinct claim supported by the inspected evidence is the exact cutoff, global basin classification, and explicit critical amplitude for the specified cubic flow with fixed periodic multiplicative removals. Strong-Allee bistability, fold mechanisms, flight-time methods and the generic parabolic 1/n rate are not claimed as original.
residual_risks: Earlier poorly indexed work on the exact scalar cubic system with fixed multiplicative pulses may exist. The inspected comparisons do not establish priority.

value.rationale: For pulse removals under depensation it matters whether any positive stock can persist at a given retention and recovery interval. The closed interval cutoff and the all-stock basins answer that question without time-stepping or fitting, and the exact one-sided rate distinguishes slow critical persistence from ordinary attraction. The amplitude and global cutoff supply predictive information beyond the generic observation that saddle nodes occur.
residual_risks: Value is as an exact deterministic benchmark, not as a recommendation of real harvest frequencies or a stochastic persistence guarantee.
